| identity | `required-open` | A motion is first-order data: a list of tracks, each a key, a change of one kind and a transition. | construction | `required-open` | A step's motion is built from the join of two pictures and a plan: what a kept thing does, how a new thing enters and how an old one leaves. A motion is then held in its step, started later thing by thing, put after another, fitted to a length, reduced to its ends, or put in stages: the kept things first, then the new things level by level, each level in a slot of its own. Open: nothing in the type of a motion says that a thing has one track at most for a property: `Motion.Single` says it as a predicate, and no function that builds a motion proves it of its result (debt D127). | semantics | `required-open` | `Track.at` is the meaning of a track: the pose of a thing at a moment, by the easing of the share of the duration that has passed, with one rounding down. `Motion.frame` is the meaning of a motion for one thing: its poses put on the still picture in the order of the tracks, a later pose of one property in place of an earlier one. `Join.drawn` says which things a reader draws at a moment of a step. `Transition.exact` and `mixExact` are the same readings in rational numbers at a rational time, and the whole-number readings are their floors. Open: the exact reading is stated at every rational time, for a value, a gap and a kept relation: no law speaks of a real time or of a limit, and a size that grows past its end has no exact form; a frame does not know a thing's own shape: `Frame.AtRest` says nothing of the shape, and a thing whose shape a track changed keeps the last one given; a thing inside a group that moves has its own frame and its group's, and no function puts the one inside the other. | laws | `required-open` | The end law: a track whose transition is over stands at the end of its change, so a step's last moment is the next picture, and with a plan that settles every thing of the new list then looks as the still picture has it. Between the two pictures: a kept edge that changes its shape by its nodes' transition stays joined to them, and a relation of both pictures is a relation of every whole moment, and of every rational time in exact numbers, where the things share one timing and the easing stays in range. In time: a delay by depth, a fit to a length, a reduction to the ends and a step in stages each keep the order that the tracks had, and in a staged step no new thing appears before the kept things are at rest. Of a thing: where no thing has two tracks of one property, its frame shows the pose of each of its tracks and does not depend on their order. Open: a fact of an easing at whole stops does not reach a transition of a duration other than a thousand, and the duration that a distance asks for has no law of order (debt D126); no law says that a thing that leaves ends as nothing: a plan's `leave` may be any change; `Motion.Same` is kept by `++` in its second part only where both rows are `Single`: the law without that premise is false, and an example of `Frame.lean` refutes it; a step in stages has no order inside one level: with lean4-effect4's shares a new edge and the box at its end overlap by a twentieth of the slot. | representation | `required-open` | An easing of two heights is the curve that CSS names `cubic-bezier(1/3, y1, 2/3, y2)`, whose first coordinate is the progress, and the reading of a transition is that polynomial at the exact share of the duration, rounded down once. A list of stops is what CSS names `linear(…)`. The writer gives each track two keyframes, a duration, a delay and its easing, filled both ways; its times are written exactly, to a thousandth of a millisecond; and a step can be opened at a moment, running or paused. Open: no law relates the written sheet to the reading: CSS animations, CSS easing functions, the individual transform properties and `d` as a property are not sealed, and the package holds no model of what a browser computes from them; debt D119.
